main_text.p: simul constituuntur res generari ex non corpore: quod sane nullus physicis rationibus assuefactus concedet.
Ergo tres hæ opiniones, de modo quo elementa generantur ex se invicem, reijciendæ sunt. Quæ autem vera retinendaq; [?]sit sententia, Aristoteles lib. 1. de Generatione abundè explicat.
main_text.head: An elementis aptè tribuantur diversæ figuræ?
main_text.p: Libro 7. cap. 8.Philosophi nonnulli, in primis autem qui dixerunt Elementa ex se invicem generari per transfigurationem, certa figurâ unicuique corpori simplici elementoq; attribuerunt, atq; cœlo quidem sphæricam, igni pyramidalem, aeri octohedrâ, aquæ εἰκο-σαέδρῳ[?], terræ verò cubicâ: hisq; ita figuratis mundum universum constare arbitrati sunt. Sed has figuras nullo pacto elementis tribui posse, haud difficile est demonstrare.

1. Si ea astruantur primorum & simplicium corporum figuræ, necessarium erit concedere aliquid actu vacuum: quod cum natura pugnat. Probatur consequentia. Tam variæ enim figuræ non replebunt omne spacium, præsertim cum non possint undequaque mutuo sese contingere atq; angulos coniungere.

page.notes: Line-end hyphen "per-" at the foot of the page continues on the next page. "Libro 7. cap. 8." is a printed margin reference, not text of the paragraph. The Greek word at "aquæ" is broken across the line end ("εἰκο-" / "σαέδρῳ") and its reading is doubtful; the Greek is reproduced as best read. "contmentis" appears to be a printing error for "continentis", left as printed. The reading "fit"/"sit" in "retinendaq; sit sententia" is uncertain. The page number is printed in old-style figures ("238"). The head "An elementis aptè tribuantur diversæ figuræ?" is an unnumbered section title set apart from the text.
